Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Albuquerque NM
1253 AM MST Sat Nov 28 2026

...New SHORT TERM, LONG TERM, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Issued at 1220 AM MST Sat Nov 28 2026
 
- Hazardous to potentially dangerous winds will produce difficult
  travel and blowing around light objects Saturday afternoon in
  central and eastern NM, focusing to eastern NM Saturday night. 

- Rain and snow looks to return to portions of western and central
  New Mexico by Tuesday night through Thursday of next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Sunday)
Issued at 1220 AM MST Sat Nov 28 2026

A strong shortwave trough will dig southeastward across the
central Rockies today, bringing a period of very gusty
northwesterly winds to much of eastern and central New Mexico by 
the late morning and throughout the afternoon. A 100-120 knot jet 
streak rounding the base of the trough, combined with favorable 
mountain wave activity and deep boundary level mixing, will help 
these strong midlevel winds to the surface. The strongest gusts up
to 60 mph are expected along and east of the central mountain 
chain, particularly across the central highlands and areas near 
Clines Corners, as well as the Johnson and Bartlett Mesas, 
including Raton Pass and Union County. Areas farther west and 
south should see comparatively lighter winds. Hazardous crosswinds
will be of concern, especially across north-south oriented 
roadways. A cold front will then surge southward across eastern 
New Mexico this evening and overnight, maintaining strong
northerly winds behind it. This will particularly be the case
across northeastern portions of the state. A brief period of light
winter precipitation cannot be ruled out near Raton Pass and the
adjacent mesas during the early evening.

Winds relax by sunrise Sunday. Strong northerly flow and cold air
advection behind the aforementioned cold front will bring a 
noticeable cooldown across eastern portions of the state on 
Sunday, with highs falling 10-25 degrees compared to Saturday. 
Central and western areas will experience a more modest 
temperature change. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Sunday night through Friday)
Issued at 1220 AM MST Sat Nov 28 2026

Quieter weather returns early next week as we transition to more
zonal flow aloft. However, a weak shortwave passing through on
Monday will bring breezy westerly winds during the afternoon. 

The main story next week will be what looks to be an impactful 
closed low traversing across the Desert Southwest during the 
Tuesday-Thursday timeframe. There is growing agreement among 
long-term model guidance and ensembles on the development of this 
low. Impacts look to begin on Tuesday as increasing southwesterly 
flow ahead of the system will bring more breezy conditions to the 
region, followed by increasing precipitation chances by Tuesday
night/Wednesday as the system makes its way inland. Current 
guidance favors more widespread rain due to warmer conditions 
ahead of the system. However, mountain snow and a mix of rain and 
snow will remain possible across western, central, and northern 
high terrain beginning Tuesday night and continuing into Thursday.
Snow levels and precipitation totals will depend on the system's 
eventual track and moisture availability. Precipitation will 
gradually taper off from west to east Thursday into Friday as the 
system exits. Although, uncertainty remains regarding the timing 
of departure. Temperatures will trend cooler behind this system.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1037 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

No major changes since the last TAF update. An upper-level trough
progressing from the northwest will push batches of thick cirrus 
across the region tonight through Saturday morning. LLWS will 
increase overnight as winds aloft strengthen. Northwest winds will
mix down by late morning to early afternoon, with peak gusts of 
25-35 knots. NBM guidance indicates a 30-60% chance that gusts 
will exceed 35 knots at KABQ after 2PM Saturday. An Airport 
Weather Warning may be warranted if guidance continues to trend 
stronger.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1220 AM MST Sat Nov 28 2026

Strong west-northwesterly winds are expected today, with the
strongest gusts reaching up to 60 mph across the central 
highlands and northeastern New Mexico. While the combination of
wind and low humidity could lead to elevated fire danger, humidity
levels and current fuel conditions should limit the overall fire
threat. Winds will shift more to the north Saturday evening into
Sunday as a cold front moves through northeast and east-central
zones, cooling things down substantially. Winds diminish early
around sunrise on Sunday before breezy conditions make another
appearance Monday and Tuesday. Guidance is in good agreement
regarding the arrival of our next system, which looks to bring
meaningful rain and snow chances during the Tuesday night-
Thursday timeframe. 

&&
